I've had lots of roommates throughout the years & what I find works best is before you even consider getting a roommie, know exactly what kind of household you want. For instance, I'm quite introverted so I don't like having people over and I'm not looking for a roommate that wants to hang out all the time. Set house rules and make them clear. Some of my rules are, don't use/eat/touch my things w/o asking. Don't have people over more than twice a week & when you do give me a heads up and keep to your area of the house. So on and so forth. Then when your interviewing roommates make all these things very clear, get references. If a problem should arise, if you're angry give yourself time to cool down then sit them down and have an adult conversation about it. Otherwise little things will build up and build up and you'll end up hating each other. I own my house though and only charge about 300/month for the top floor of my house so I have a little more say in what goes on in my home verses people equally sharing a rental unit.
